Method of Attack: Acts as an infection funnel using a single Windows executable to launch a dozen different malware families simultaneously
Drops dozens of malware families and launches them using a hardcoded list and Windows cmd.exe tool
Infects Windows devices through fake software cracks promoted on malicious sites in Google Search results
Uses black hat SEO to promote fake game cracks and pirated software activators in high Google search results
Distributes malware via password-protected ZIP archives containing the dropper
Relies on users bypassing AV warnings and executing unsigned executables manually
Impacted Systems: Customers across United States, Germany, France, Italy, India, Russia, Brazil, Turkey, and Egypt
Attack Vector: Fake software cracks and pirated software activators downloaded from malicious websites found via Google Search
Password-protected ZIP archives containing the NullMixer dropper
Manual execution of unsigned and potentially dangerous executables by users
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious websites promoting fake cracks appearing in second, third, and fourth Google search results for 'software crack'
Password-protected ZIP archives downloaded from malicious sites
